newsitem.title: USA: Mallinckrodt sees $100 mln savings in deal.
newsitem.headline: Mallinckrodt sees $100 mln savings in deal.

text.p: Mallinckrodt Inc said it anticipates $100 million in cost savings in fiscal 1999 from its proposed $1.9 billion acquisition of medical device company Nellcor Puritan Bennett Inc.

Although the proposed deal will expand Mallinckrodt's role in the growing industry, Mallinckrodt chief executive officer Ray Holman said the deal's financial success is based on cost savings, not revenue enhancement.
Holman made his remarks in a morning meeting and conference call with Wall Street analysts. A tape recording of the call was made available.
The cash transaction will be financed by $700 million in cash raised from recent divestitures and a new $1.2 billion credit facility. Holman said all the financing is in place.
Holman also said the companies do not expect any antitrust issues to block the transaction.
"There is virtually no competition between the two companies," he said, adding that the product lines are complementary but do not overlap.

Mallinckrodt chief financial officer Michael Rocca said the company expects charges of $325 million to $600 million in fiscal 1998 from the transaction. Excluding the charges, the deal is expected to dilute earnings by 15 percent in fiscal 1998 and boost earnings by 10 to 15 percent in fiscal 1999.
Rocca also said the company expects to book $1.2 to $1.4 billion in goodwill from the transaction.
